title: Long-Context Modeling with Dynamic Hierarchical Sparse Attention for Memory-Constrained LLM Inference
claim: A plug-in module predicts sparsity hierarchically, from token boundaries to chunk similarity to indices, and slots into a standard transformer block.
layout: 2 panels: transformer block at right, zoomed 4-step pipeline at left, dashed callout
description: The figure has two parts. On the right is a transformer layer in a gray rounded box labeled ×N. It contains Multi-Head Attention, Add & Norm, Feed Forward, and Add & Norm, with residual arrows. Input tokens t0..t13 sit at the bottom as colored blocks, with positional encoding added through a ⊕. The output is labeled Output embeddings. A bright yellow box, 'Our Proposed DHSA module', feeds into attention. A dashed yellow arrow links it to a large dashed yellow panel on the left, titled 'Dynamic Hierarchical Sparsity Prediction'. That panel shows four steps from bottom to top. Step 1 is boundary prediction: tokens split by red dashed lines b0..b6. Step 2 is chunk aggregation: chunks C0..C5. Step 3 is dot-product similarity: a grayscale chunk-similarity matrix. Step 4 is index routing and TopK selection: lists of selected key indices per query chunk. Colors group tokens into chunks. The eye goes first to the yellow module.
caption: Performance of DHSA on LLaMA-3.1-8B (4-bit). (a) Needle-in-a-Haystack accuracy under a fixed density of 6.25%, where DHSA preserves high retrieval accuracy up to 100K context length. (b) Time-to-first-token (TTFT) on a single NVIDIA RTX 3090 (24\,GB). DHSA scales to long contexts while remaining feasible in memory-constrained settings.
abstract: The quadratic cost of attention limits the scalability of long-context LLMs, especially under limited hardware memory budgets. While attention is often sparse, existing static sparse methods cannot adapt to task- or input-dependent variations, and recent dynamic approaches rely on predefined templates or heuristics that may sacrifice generality. We propose Dynamic Hierarchical Sparse Attention (DHSA), a data-driven framework that predicts attention sparsity online while keeping the LLM backbone frozen. DHSA performs hierarchical routing by estimating importance at the chunk level and propagating it to token-level interactions, preserving causally important dependencies while enabling efficient sparsification. Across Needle-in-a-Haystack test, LongBench and RULER, DHSA maintains near-dense accuracy in highly sparse regimes, achieving 12--20% relative accuracy gains over Block Sparse Attention at comparable prefill cost. With a memory-efficient tiled backend, DHSA delivers up to $10\times$ prefill speedup at 128K context length. On LLaMA-3.1-8B (4-bit), DHSA scales to 100K context on a single 24GB GPU, where dense attention fails. We provide complementary GPU and CPU backends, enabling DHSA to run across diverse hardware environments and multiple open-weight model families. These results demonstrate DHSA as an efficient and adaptable solution for memory-constrained long-context LLM inference.
